sanskrit: amaṅgalyadhvaje tasmin strīpūrve ca viśeṣataḥ na prahartum abhīpsāmi gṛhīteṣuṃ kathaṃ cana
english: Against one who bears that inauspicious banner, and above all against one who was formerly a woman, I have no wish to strike, nor in any way to take up my arrows.

sanskrit: tad antaraṃ samāsādya pāṇḍavo māṃ dhanaṃjayaḥ śarair ghātayatu kṣipraṃ samantād bharatarṣabha
english: Seizing that opening, let the Pāṇḍava Dhanaṃjaya swiftly strike me down with his arrows from every side, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: na taṃ paśyāmi lokeṣu yo māṃ hanyāt samudyatam ṛte kṛṣṇān mahābhāgāt pāṇḍavād vā dhanaṃjayāt
english: In all the worlds I see no one who could slay me when I stand ready for battle, save the illustrious Kṛṣṇa, or the Pāṇḍava Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: eṣa tasmāt purodhāya kaṃ cid anyaṃ mamāgrataḥ māṃ pātayatu bībhatsur evaṃ te vijayo bhavet
english: Therefore, placing some other before me in the van, let Bībhatsu strike me down — thus shall victory be yours.

sanskrit: etat kuruṣva kaunteya yathoktaṃ vacanaṃ mama tato jeṣyasi saṃgrāme dhārtarāṣṭrān samāgatān
english: Do this, son of Kuntī, as I have said in my words; then in battle you shall conquer the assembled sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca te 'nujñātās tataḥ pārthā jagmuḥ svaśibiraṃ prati abhivādya mahātmānaṃ bhīṣmaṃ kurupitāmaham
english: Saṃjaya said: Granted leave, the sons of Pṛthā then went toward their own camp, having saluted the great-souled Bhīṣma, grandsire of the Kurus.

sanskrit: tathoktavati gāṅgeye paralokāya dīkṣite arjuno duḥkhasaṃtaptaḥ savrīḍam idam abravīt
english: When the son of Gaṅgā, now consecrated for the other world, had spoken thus, Arjuna, burning with grief, said this with shame:

sanskrit: guruṇā kulavṛddhena kṛtaprajñena dhīmatā pitāmahena saṃgrāme kathaṃ yotsyāmi mādhava
english: With my teacher, the elder of our house, the wise and discerning grandsire — how shall I fight him in battle, O Mādhava?

sanskrit: krīḍatā hi mayā bālye vāsudeva mahāmanāḥ pāṃsurūṣitagātreṇa mahātmā paruṣīkṛtaḥ
english: For in my childhood, Vāsudeva, while I played with my limbs all smeared with dust, I roughly handled that high-minded, great-souled one.

sanskrit: yasyāham adhiruhyāṅkaṃ bālaḥ kila gadāgraja tātety avocaṃ pitaraṃ pituḥ pāṇḍor mahātmanaḥ
english: Climbing onto his lap as a child, O elder brother of Gada, I would call him 'Father,' though he was the father of my own father, the great-souled Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: nāhaṃ tātas tava pitus tāto 'smi tava bhārata iti mām abravīd bālye yaḥ sa vadhyaḥ kathaṃ mayā
english: 'I am not your father, but your father's father, O Bhārata' — so he said to me in my childhood. How is such a one to be slain by me?

sanskrit: kāmaṃ vadhyatu me sainyaṃ nāhaṃ yotsye mahātmanā jayo vāstu vadho vā me kathaṃ vā kṛṣṇa manyase
english: Let my army be slain if it must — I will not fight the great-souled one. Be it victory or death for me, what is your judgment, O Kṛṣṇa?

sanskrit: śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca pratijñāya vadhaṃ jiṣṇo purā bhīṣmasya saṃyuge kṣatradharme sthitaḥ pārtha kathaṃ nainaṃ haniṣyasi
english: The blessed Kṛṣṇa said: Having vowed before, O Jiṣṇu, to slay Bhīṣma in battle, and standing fast in the duty of a warrior, O Pārtha, how will you not slay him?

sanskrit: pātayainaṃ rathāt pārtha vajrāhatam iva drumam nāhatvā yudhi gāṅgeyaṃ vijayas te bhaviṣyati
english: Cast him down from his chariot, O Pārtha, like a tree struck by the thunderbolt. Without slaying the son of Gaṅgā in battle, no victory shall be yours.

sanskrit: diṣṭam etat purā devair bhaviṣyaty avaśasya te hantā bhīṣmasya pūrvendra iti tan na tad anyathā
english: This was ordained of old by the gods, and shall come to pass beyond your control: 'The slayer of Bhīṣma shall be the former Indra' — and that cannot be otherwise.

sanskrit: na hi bhīṣmaṃ durādharṣaṃ vyāttānanam ivāntakam tvad anyaḥ śaknuyād dhantum api vajradharaḥ svayam
english: For Bhīṣma, unassailable, like Death with gaping jaws — none other than you could slay him, not even the wielder of the thunderbolt himself.

sanskrit: jahi bhīṣmaṃ mahābāho śṛṇu cedaṃ vaco mama yathovāca purā śakraṃ mahābuddhir bṛhaspatiḥ
english: Slay Bhīṣma, mighty-armed one, and hear this word of mine, even as the deeply wise Bṛhaspati once spoke to Śakra:

sanskrit: jyāyāṃsam api cec chakra guṇair api samanvitam ātatāyinam āmantrya hanyād ghātakam āgatam
english: 'Even an elder, O Śakra, even one endowed with virtues, if he comes as an assassin bent on murder, one may challenge and slay him.'

sanskrit: śāśvato 'yaṃ sthito dharmaḥ kṣatriyāṇāṃ dhanaṃjaya yoddhavyaṃ rakṣitavyaṃ ca yaṣṭavyaṃ cānasūyubhiḥ
english: This is the eternal, established law of warriors, O Dhanaṃjaya: that without malice they must fight, must protect, and must offer sacrifice.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca śikhaṇḍī nidhanaṃ kṛṣṇa bhīṣmasya bhavitā dhruvam dṛṣṭvaiva hi sadā bhīṣmaḥ pāñcālyaṃ vinivartate
english: Arjuna said: Śikhaṇḍin shall surely be the death of Bhīṣma, O Kṛṣṇa; for the moment Bhīṣma sees the Pāñcāla prince, he always turns away.

sanskrit: te vayaṃ pramukhe tasya sthāpayitvā śikhaṇḍinam gāṅgeyaṃ pātayiṣyāma upāyeneti me matiḥ
english: So we, stationing Śikhaṇḍin at the forefront before him, shall cast down the son of Gaṅgā by this stratagem — such is my thought.

sanskrit: aham anyān maheṣvāsān vārayiṣyāmi sāyakaiḥ śikhaṇḍy api yudhāṃ śreṣṭho bhīṣmam evābhiyāsyatu
english: I shall hold off the other great archers with my shafts, while Śikhaṇḍin, foremost of fighters, advances against Bhīṣma alone.

sanskrit: śrutaṃ te kurumukhyasya nāhaṃ hanyāṃ śikhaṇḍinam kanyā hy eṣā purā jātā puruṣaḥ samapadyata
english: You have heard the chief of the Kurus say, 'I will not slay Śikhaṇḍin, for he was born a maiden of old and only afterward became a man.'

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca ity evaṃ niścayaṃ kṛtvā pāṇḍavāḥ sahamādhavāḥ śayanāni yathāsvāni bhejire puruṣarṣabhāḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Having reached this resolve, the Pāṇḍavas together with Mādhava, those bulls among men, each repaired to his own couch.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca kathaṃ śikhaṇḍī gāṅgeyam abhyavartata saṃyuge pāṇḍavāś ca tathā bhīṣmaṃ tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: How did Śikhaṇḍin advance against the son of Gaṅgā in battle, and how did the Pāṇḍavas advance against Bhīṣma? Tell me that, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tataḥ prabhāte vimale sūryasyodayanaṃ prati vādyamānāsu bherīṣu mṛdaṅgeṣv ānakeṣu ca
english: Saṃjaya said: Then, when the clear dawn came toward the rising of the sun, while kettledrums, tabors, and war-drums were being sounded,

sanskrit: dhmāyatsu dadhivarṇeṣu jalajeṣu samantataḥ śikhaṇḍinaṃ puraskṛtya niryātāḥ pāṇḍavā yudhi
english: and while curd-white conches were being blown on every side, the Pāṇḍavas, placing Śikhaṇḍin at their head, marched forth to battle.

sanskrit: kṛtvā vyūhaṃ mahārāja sarvaśatrunibarhaṇam śikhaṇḍī sarvasainyānām agra āsīd viśāṃ pate
english: Having formed an array, great king, that could crush every foe, Śikhaṇḍin stood at the forefront of all the troops, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: cakrarakṣau tatas tasya bhīmasenadhanaṃjayau pṛṣṭhato draupadeyāś ca saubhadraś caiva vīryavān
english: As guardians of his chariot-wheels were Bhīmasena and Dhanaṃjaya, and behind came the sons of Draupadī and the valiant son of Subhadrā.

sanskrit: sātyakiś cekitānaś ca teṣāṃ goptā mahārathaḥ dhṛṣṭadyumnas tataḥ paścāt pāñcālair abhirakṣitaḥ
english: Sātyaki and Cekitāna, the great car-warrior, were their protectors; and behind came Dhṛṣṭadyumna, guarded by the Pāñcālas.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā yamābhyāṃ sahitaḥ prabhuḥ prayayau siṃhanādena nādayan bharatarṣabha
english: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira, the lord, together with the twins, advanced, making the field resound with his lion's roar, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: virāṭas tu tataḥ paścāt svena sainyena saṃvṛtaḥ drupadaś ca mahārāja tataḥ paścād upādravat
english: Behind them came Virāṭa, surrounded by his own army, and after him, great king, Drupada pressed forward.

sanskrit: kekayā bhrātaraḥ pañca dhṛṣṭaketuś ca vīryavān jaghanaṃ pālayām āsa pāṇḍusainyasya bhārata
english: The five Kekaya brothers and the valiant Dhṛṣṭaketu guarded the rear of the Pāṇḍava host, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: evaṃ vyūhya mahat sainyaṃ pāṇḍavās tava vāhinīm abhyadravanta saṃgrāme tyaktvā jīvitam ātmanaḥ
english: Having thus arrayed their great army, the Pāṇḍavas charged upon your host in battle, casting aside their very lives.

sanskrit: tathaiva kuravo rājan bhīṣmaṃ kṛtvā mahābalam agrataḥ sarvasainyānāṃ prayayuḥ pāṇḍavān prati
english: In like manner the Kurus, O king, placing the mighty Bhīṣma at the head of all their troops, marched out against the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: putrais tava durādharṣai rakṣitaḥ sumahābalaiḥ tato droṇo maheṣvāsaḥ putraś cāsya mahārathaḥ
english: Guarded by your sons, unassailable and of great might, came Droṇa the great archer, and his son the great car-warrior;

sanskrit: bhagadattas tataḥ paścād gajānīkena saṃvṛtaḥ kṛpaś ca kṛtavarmā ca bhagadattam anuvratau
english: behind them Bhagadatta, surrounded by a host of elephants, and Kṛpa and Kṛtavarman, devoted followers of Bhagadatta.

sanskrit: kāmbojarājo balavāṃs tataḥ paścāt sudakṣiṇaḥ māgadhaś ca jayatsenaḥ saubalaś ca bṛhadbalaḥ
english: Behind them the mighty king of the Kāmbojas, Sudakṣiṇa, and Jayatsena of Magadha, and the son of Subala, and Bṛhadbala.

sanskrit: tathetare maheṣvāsāḥ suśarmapramukhā nṛpāḥ jaghanaṃ pālayām āsus tava sainyasya bhārata
english: And the other great archers, kings led by Suśarman, guarded the rear of your army, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: divase divase prāpte bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavo yudhi āsurān akarod vyūhān paiśācān atha rākṣasān
english: Day after day, as it came, Bhīṣma the son of Śaṃtanu formed in battle arrays after the manner of the Asuras, the Piśācas, and the Rākṣasas.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ tava teṣāṃ ca bhārata anyonyaṃ nighnatāṃ rājan yamarāṣṭravivardhanam
english: Then began the battle between your men and theirs, O Bhārata, as they struck one another down, O king — a battle that swelled the realm of Yama.

sanskrit: arjunapramukhāḥ pārthāḥ puraskṛtya śikhaṇḍinam bhīṣmaṃ yuddhe 'bhyavartanta kiranto vividhāñ śarān
english: The sons of Pṛthā, led by Arjuna, placing Śikhaṇḍin before them, advanced upon Bhīṣma in battle, scattering arrows of every kind.

sanskrit: tatra bhārata bhīmena pīḍitās tāvakāḥ śaraiḥ rudhiraughapariklinnāḥ paralokaṃ yayus tadā
english: There, O Bhārata, your warriors, sorely pressed by Bhīma's arrows and drenched in streams of blood, went then to the other world.

sanskrit: nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca sātyakiś ca mahārathaḥ tava sainyaṃ samāsādya pīḍayām āsur ojasā
english: Nakula and Sahadeva and Sātyaki the great car-warrior, falling upon your army, harried it with their might.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānāḥ samare tāvakā bharatarṣabha nāśaknuvan vārayituṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ mahad balam
english: Being slaughtered in the battle, your men, O bull of the Bharatas, were unable to hold back the great force of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: tatas tu tāvakaṃ sainyaṃ vadhyamānaṃ samantataḥ saṃprādravad diśo rājan kālyamānaṃ mahārathaiḥ
english: Then your army, cut down on every side, O king, fled in all directions, driven on by the great car-warriors.

sanskrit: trātāraṃ nādhyagacchanta tāvakā bharatarṣabha vadhyamānāḥ śitair bāṇaiḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ sahasṛñjayaiḥ
english: Your men found no rescuer, O bull of the Bharatas, as they were struck down by the sharp arrows of the Pāṇḍavas and the Sṛñjayas.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca pīḍyamānaṃ balaṃ pārthair dṛṣṭvā bhīṣmaḥ parākramī yad akārṣīd raṇe kruddhas tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Seeing his army hard pressed by the sons of Pṛthā, what did the valiant Bhīṣma do in his wrath upon the field? Tell me that, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: kathaṃ vā pāṇḍavān yuddhe pratyudyātaḥ paraṃtapaḥ vinighnan somakān vīrāṃs tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: And how did that scorcher of foes advance against the Pāṇḍavas in battle, striking down the heroic Somakas? Tell me that, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca ācakṣe te mahārāja yad akārṣīt pitāmahaḥ pīḍite tava putrasya sainye pāṇḍavasṛñjayaiḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: I will tell you, great king, what the grandsire did when your son's army was hard pressed by the Pāṇḍavas and the Sṛñjayas.

sanskrit: prahṛṣṭamanasaḥ śūrāḥ pāṇḍavāḥ pāṇḍupūrvaja abhyavartanta nighnantas tava putrasya vāhinīm
english: With gladdened hearts the heroic Pāṇḍavas, O elder of Pāṇḍu's line, advanced, smiting your son's host.

sanskrit: taṃ vināśaṃ manuṣyendra naravāraṇavājinām nāmṛṣyata tadā bhīṣmaḥ sainyaghātaṃ raṇe paraiḥ
english: That destruction of men, elephants, and horses, O lord of men — that slaughter of his army by the foe in battle — Bhīṣma could not then endure.

sanskrit: sa pāṇḍavān maheṣvāsaḥ pāñcālāṃś ca sasṛñjayān abhyadravata durdharṣas tyaktvā jīvitam ātmanaḥ
english: That unassailable great archer charged upon the Pāṇḍavas and the Pāñcālas together with the Sṛñjayas, casting aside his own life.

sanskrit: sa pāṇḍavānāṃ pravarān pañca rājan mahārathān āttaśastrān raṇe yattān vārayām āsa sāyakaiḥ nārācair vatsadantaiś ca śitair añjalikais tathā
english: He held off the five foremost car-warriors of the Pāṇḍavas, O king, who stood ready with weapons raised in battle, with his shafts — with iron arrows, with calf-tooth darts, and with sharp crescent-headed barbs.

sanskrit: nijaghne samare kruddho hastyaśvam amitaṃ bahu rathino 'pātayad rājan rathebhyaḥ puruṣarṣabhaḥ
english: In his wrath he slew in battle countless elephants and horses beyond measure, and that bull among men hurled the chariot-warriors down from their cars, O king.

sanskrit: sādinaś cāśvapṛṣṭhebhyaḥ padātīṃś ca samāgatān gajārohān gajebhyaś ca pareṣāṃ vidadhad bhayam
english: He cast the riders from the backs of their horses and the foot-soldiers that closed with him, and the elephant-riders from their elephants, spreading terror among the foe.

sanskrit: tam ekaṃ samare bhīṣmaṃ tvaramāṇaṃ mahāratham pāṇḍavāḥ samavartanta vajrapāṇim ivāsurāḥ
english: Against that single Bhīṣma, the great car-warrior pressing swiftly on in battle, the Pāṇḍavas closed in, as the Asuras against the wielder of the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: śakrāśanisamasparśān vimuñcan niśitāñ śarān dikṣv adṛśyata sarvāsu ghoraṃ saṃdhārayan vapuḥ
english: Loosing sharp arrows whose touch was like Indra's thunderbolt, he was seen in every quarter, bearing a terrible form.

sanskrit: maṇḍalīkṛtam evāsya nityaṃ dhanur adṛśyata saṃgrāme yudhyamānasya śakracāpanibhaṃ mahat
english: As he fought in the battle, his great bow, like the bow of Indra, was seen forever drawn into a perfect circle.

sanskrit: tad dṛṣṭvā samare karma tava putrā viśāṃ pate vismayaṃ paramaṃ prāptāḥ pitāmaham apūjayan
english: Seeing that feat in battle, your sons, O lord of peoples, were filled with the highest wonder and did honor to the grandsire.

sanskrit: pārthā vimanaso bhūtvā praikṣanta pitaraṃ tava yudhyamānaṃ raṇe śūraṃ vipracittim ivāmarāḥ na cainaṃ vārayām āsur vyāttānanam ivāntakam
english: The sons of Pṛthā, grown downcast, gazed upon your sire, that hero fighting in the field, as the immortals once gazed upon Vipracitti; nor could they stay him, who was like Death with gaping jaws.

sanskrit: daśame 'hani saṃprāpte rathānīkaṃ śikhaṇḍinaḥ adahan niśitair bāṇaiḥ kṛṣṇavartmeva kānanam
english: When the tenth day had come, he consumed Śikhaṇḍin's host of chariots with his sharp arrows, as the fire whose path is black consumes a forest.

sanskrit: taṃ śikhaṇḍī tribhir bāṇair abhyavidhyat stanāntare āśīviṣam iva kruddhaṃ kālasṛṣṭam ivāntakam
english: Śikhaṇḍin pierced him with three arrows between the breasts — him who was like an enraged venomous serpent, like Death sent forth by Time.

sanskrit: sa tenātibhṛśaṃ viddhaḥ prekṣya bhīṣmaḥ śikhaṇḍinam anicchann api saṃkruddhaḥ prahasann idam abravīt
english: Pierced thus most grievously, Bhīṣma, looking upon Śikhaṇḍin, though unwilling and wroth, said this with a laugh:

sanskrit: kāmam abhyasa vā mā vā na tvāṃ yotsye kathaṃ cana yaiva hi tvaṃ kṛtā dhātrā saiva hi tvaṃ śikhaṇḍinī
english: "Strike me if you will or do not — in no wise shall I fight you; for you remain the very Śikhaṇḍinī that the Creator made you."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā śikhaṇḍī krodhamūrchitaḥ uvāca bhīṣmaṃ samare sṛkkiṇī parilelihan
english: Hearing that speech of his, Śikhaṇḍin, swooning with rage, licking the corners of his mouth, said to Bhīṣma in the battle:

sanskrit: jānāmi tvāṃ mahābāho kṣatriyāṇāṃ kṣayaṃkaram mayā śrutaṃ ca te yuddhaṃ jāmadagnyena vai saha
english: "I know you, mighty-armed one, as the bringer of doom to the warriors; and I have heard of your battle with the son of Jamadagni.

sanskrit: divyaś ca te prabhāvo 'yaṃ sa mayā bahuśaḥ śrutaḥ jānann api prabhāvaṃ te yotsye 'dyāhaṃ tvayā saha
english: This divine might of yours I have heard of many times; yet, knowing your might, I shall this day do battle with you.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavānāṃ priyaṃ kurvann ātmanaś ca narottama adya tvā yodhayiṣyāmi raṇe puruṣasattama
english: Doing what pleases the Pāṇḍavas and myself, O best of men, this day I shall fight you in battle, O most excellent of men.

sanskrit: dhruvaṃ ca tvā haniṣyāmi śape satyena te 'grataḥ etac chrutvā vaco mahyaṃ yat kṣamaṃ tat samācara
english: And surely I shall slay you — I swear it by truth before your face. Having heard this word of mine, do whatever you deem fit."

sanskrit: kāmam abhyasa vā mā vā na me jīvan vimokṣyase sudṛṣṭaḥ kriyatāṃ bhīṣma loko 'yaṃ samitiṃjaya
english: "Strike me if you will or do not — you shall not escape me alive. Look well upon this world, O Bhīṣma, victor in battle!"

sanskrit: evam uktvā tato bhīṣmaṃ pañcabhir nataparvabhiḥ avidhyata raṇe rājan praṇunnaṃ vākyasāyakaiḥ
english: Having spoken thus, he then pierced Bhīṣma in the battle, O king, with five straight-jointed arrows, after first driving home his shafts of words.

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā savyasācī paraṃtapaḥ kālo 'yam iti saṃcintya śikhaṇḍinam acodayat
english: Hearing those words of his, the ambidextrous one, scorcher of foes, thinking 'This is the hour,' urged Śikhaṇḍin on:

sanskrit: ahaṃ tvām anuyāsyāmi parān vidrāvayañ śaraiḥ abhidrava susaṃrabdho bhīṣmaṃ bhīmaparākramam
english: "I shall follow close behind you, scattering the foe with my arrows. Charge, in furious wrath, upon Bhīṣma of terrible valor.

sanskrit: na hi te saṃyuge pīḍāṃ śaktaḥ kartuṃ mahābalaḥ tasmād adya mahābāho vīra bhīṣmam abhidrava
english: For the mighty one is not able to do you harm in battle; therefore this day, O mighty-armed hero, charge upon Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: ahatvā samare bhīṣmaṃ yadi yāsyasi māriṣa avahāsyo 'sya lokasya bhaviṣyasi mayā saha
english: If without slaying Bhīṣma in battle you turn away, good sir, you shall become, along with me, the laughingstock of this world.

sanskrit: nāvahāsyā yathā vīra bhavema paramāhave tathā kuru raṇe yatnaṃ sādhayasva pitāmaham
english: That we may not become objects of mockery, O hero, in this great battle, so put forth your effort in the fight: bring down the grandsire.

sanskrit: ahaṃ te rakṣaṇaṃ yuddhe kariṣyāmi paraṃtapa vārayan rathinaḥ sarvān sādhayasva pitāmaham
english: I shall be your guard in the battle, O scorcher of foes, holding off all the chariot-warriors: bring down the grandsire.

sanskrit: droṇaṃ ca droṇaputraṃ ca kṛpaṃ cātha suyodhanam citrasenaṃ vikarṇaṃ ca saindhavaṃ ca jayadratham
english: Droṇa and Droṇa's son, and Kṛpa, and Suyodhana, and Citrasena and Vikarṇa, and the lord of Sindhu, Jayadratha,

sanskrit: vindānuvindāv āvantyau kāmbojaṃ ca sudakṣiṇam bhagadattaṃ tathā śūraṃ māgadhaṃ ca mahāratham
english: Vinda and Anuvinda of Avanti, and Sudakṣiṇa the Kāmboja, and the heroic Bhagadatta, and the Māgadha, the great car-warrior —"
